subject: Mathematics
source: Drive: Maths folder (SoW Maths, GCSE Maths folder and revision materials); Edexcel GCSE Mathematics (1MA1) specification, Higher tier content

lessons.title: Completing the square
objectives: Write x² + bx + c in the form (x + p)² + q
Complete the square when the coefficient of x² is not 1
Check answers by expanding

keywords.def: rewriting a quadratic in the form (x + p)² + q
an expression that is a bracket squared, such as (x + 3)²
the number in front of a letter

teach.heading: Why completing the square?
bullets: Writes a quadratic using one x only.
Solves equations that do not factorise.
teach.note: Recall that (x + 3)² = x² + 6x + 9. So x² + 6x is 'nearly' a perfect square: it needs +9. Draw an x by x square plus two 3 by x rectangles; the missing corner is 3 by 3.

teach.heading: The method
teach.note: Write (x + 3)² and then subtract the extra 9 that the bracket creates. Check by expanding: (x + 3)² − 2 = x² + 6x + 9 − 2 = x² + 6x + 7 ✓.

teach.heading: Negative middle term
bullets: The bracket sign matches the sign of b.
teach.note: Half of −8 is −4. Subtract 16, not −16. Check at x = 0: left 3; right 16 − 13 = 3 ✓. Misconception: writing (x − 4)² + 13.

teach.heading: Odd coefficient
teach.note: Fractions are fine. Alternative decimal form: (x + 2.5)² − 6.25. Ask: why is the subtracted amount always the square of the halved number?

teach.heading: Coefficient of x² not 1 (Higher)
teach.note: Take out the 2 from x² and x terms only, complete the square inside, then multiply the −9 by 2: −18 + 5 = −13. Check at x = 0: 2 × 9 − 13 = 5 ✓.

practice: Write x² + 10x + 3 in the form (x + a)² + b.
Write x² − 4x + 9 in the form (x + a)² + b.
Write x² + 3x + 1 in the form (x + a)² + b.
independent: Complete the square: x² + 12x + 40 and x² − 6x − 7.
Complete the square: x² − x + 1.
Higher: write 3x² − 12x + 5 in the form a(x + p)² + q.
lessons.homework: Complete the square for six quadratics of your choice and check each by expanding.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: area model with algebra tiles and a template for (x + p)² + q. Stretch: write 2x² − 8x + 3 in completed-square form.

lessons.title: Completed square form: solving and turning points
objectives: Solve quadratic equations by completing the square
Find the turning point of a quadratic graph
State the line of symmetry

keywords.def: the minimum or maximum point of a quadratic graph
the vertical line through the turning point
a root that cannot be written as an exact fraction, such as √2

teach.heading: Solving by completing the square
teach.note: Square-root both sides, remembering ±. In decimals: x = −3 + 1.414 = −1.59 and x = −3 − 1.414 = −4.41 (2 d.p.). Leave answers as surds when asked for an exact answer.

teach.heading: Another example
teach.note: Check using the quadratic formula: (4 ± √20) ÷ 2 = 2 ± √5 ✓. Compare methods: completing the square always works and gives the formula.

teach.heading: Turning point
bullets: y = (x + p)² + q has turning point (−p, q).
teach.note: A squared bracket is at least 0, so the smallest value is q when x + p = 0. Note the sign change in p. The line of symmetry is x = 4.

teach.heading: Negative x² term
bullets: The bracket term is subtracted, so there is a maximum.
teach.note: Show the steps: −(x² + 4x) + 5 = −[(x + 2)² − 4] + 5 = −(x + 2)² + 9. Check at x = 0: 9 − 4 = 5 ✓. The graph is an upside-down U shape.

teach.heading: Sketching
teach.note: For y = x² − 8x + 3: y-intercept 3, turning point (4, −13). The curve crosses the x-axis at 4 ± √13 ≈ 0.39 and 7.61. Ask pupils to check using the quadratic formula.

practice: Solve x² + 6x − 4 = 0 by completing the square (2 d.p.).
Find the turning point of y = x² + 10x + 3.
State the line of symmetry of y = (x − 4)² − 13.
independent: Solve x² − 8x + 5 = 0 exactly, then to 2 d.p.
Find the turning point of y = x² − 2x − 5 and state if it is a maximum or minimum.
Find the maximum value of y = 7 + 6x − x².
exit: Write x² + 4x + 9 in the form (x + a)² + b.
State the turning point of y = x² + 4x + 9.
lessons.homework: Sketch the graphs of two quadratics, marking the turning points and intercepts, using completed-square form.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: worked example template. Stretch: find the equation of the quadratic with minimum point (3, −2) passing through (0, 7).

lessons.title: Algebraic fractions
objectives: Simplify algebraic fractions by factorising
Multiply and divide algebraic fractions
Add and subtract algebraic fractions

keywords.def: a fraction with algebra in the numerator or denominator
divide the top and bottom by the same factor
a shared multiple of the denominators

teach.heading: Simplifying
bullets: Factorise top and bottom, then cancel.
teach.note: Only cancel factors, never terms. Misconception: (x + 3)/3 = x. Test with x = 6: 9/3 = 3, not 6. Cancel brackets only if they are multiplied.

teach.heading: Quadratic fractions
teach.note: Factorise both numerator and denominator fully. The difference of two squares in the denominator is key. Check with x = 5: the original is (25 + 25 + 6)/(25 − 9) = 56/16 = 3.5 and (x + 2)/(x − 3) = 7/2 = 3.5 ✓.

teach.heading: Multiplying and dividing
bullets: Multiply tops and bottoms after factorising.
To divide, multiply by the reciprocal.
teach.note: Cancel across numerators and denominators before multiplying. Example for division: (x² − 1)/(x + 3) ÷ (x + 1)/(x + 3) = (x − 1)(x + 1)/(x + 3) × (x + 3)/(x + 1) = x − 1.

teach.heading: Adding and subtracting
teach.note: Expand the numerators carefully: 4x + 4 + 3x − 6 = 7x − 2. Check with x = 2: 1 + 0 = 1 and 12/12 = 1 ✓.

teach.heading: Different linear denominators
teach.note: Multiply each fraction by the missing factor. Check with x = 1: 2 + 1.5 = 3.5 and 7/2 = 3.5 ✓. Leave the denominator factorised.

practice: Simplify (2x² + 6x)/(4x).
Simplify (x² − x − 12)/(x² − 16).
independent: Simplify (x² + 4x)/(x² − 16).
Add and simplify 3/(x − 1) + 2/(x + 2).
Multiply and simplify (x² − 9)/(x + 4) × (x + 4)/(x + 3).
lessons.homework: Check each of your answers by substituting x = 2 or x = 3 into the original and simplified forms.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: factorising prompts and a cancelling checklist. Stretch: solve 3/(x − 1) + 2/(x + 2) = 1.

lessons.title: Surds
objectives: Simplify surds
Expand brackets containing surds
Rationalise the denominator

keywords.def: an irrational root that cannot be written exactly as a fraction
remove the surd from the denominator
a number that cannot be written as a fraction of two integers

starter: List the square numbers up to 100.

teach.heading: What is a surd?
teach.note: A calculator shows √2 = 1.41421... which goes on without repeating, so the exact value is √2. Ask: is √16 a surd? Why not? Rules: √a × √b = √(ab) and (√a)² = a.

teach.heading: Simplifying
teach.note: List square factors: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36... √72 has factor 36: √72 = 6√2. Ask: why not 2√18 or 3√8? They are not fully simplified.

teach.heading: Adding and multiplying
teach.note: Only add surds with the same surd part, like like terms. Simplify first. Misconception: √2 + √3 = √5.

teach.heading: Expanding brackets
teach.note: Use the grid method as with algebra. The first example is a difference of two squares, so the surd terms cancel. Check numerically: (3 + 1.414)² = 19.485 and 11 + 8.485 = 19.485 ✓.

teach.heading: Rationalising
teach.note: For a two-term denominator, multiply by the conjugate (change the sign). (√5 + 2)(√5 − 2) = 5 − 4 = 1. Check: 1/4.236 = 0.236 and √5 − 2 = 0.236 ✓.

practice: Simplify √75 and √45.
Simplify √48 + √12.
Rationalise 10/√5.
independent: Expand and simplify (1 + √5)(3 − √5).
Rationalise 4/(3 − √5).
A square has area 98 cm². Write its side length in the form a√b.
lessons.homework: Write down six surds, simplify them, then check each simplification with a calculator.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: square number list and factor tree support. Stretch: show that (√5 + √2)² − 2√10 is rational.

lessons.title: The sine rule
objectives: Label a non-right-angled triangle with sides a, b, c and angles A, B, C
Use the sine rule to find a missing side
Use the sine rule to find a missing angle

keywords.def: a ÷ sin A = b ÷ sin B = c ÷ sin C
side a is opposite angle A, and so on
an angle measured clockwise from north

starter: Find θ if sin θ = 0.7 (1 d.p.).
Angles in a triangle add to what?

teach.heading: Labelling
bullets: Capital letters are angles; small letters are sides.
Side a is opposite angle A.
Use for triangles without a right angle.
teach.note: Draw a scalene triangle and label it. SOH CAH TOA only works with a right angle; the sine and cosine rules work in any triangle. Check calculator mode is degrees.

teach.heading: The sine rule
bullets: a ÷ sin A = b ÷ sin B.
Use it when you know a side and its opposite angle.
For angles, flip: sin A ÷ a = sin B ÷ b.
teach.note: You need a matching pair: a side with its opposite angle. Without a pair, use the cosine rule. Third angle: subtract the others from 180° if needed.

teach.heading: Finding a side
teach.note: Larger angle opposite the larger side: 65° > 40° so b > a ✓. Second example: A = 55°, B = 70°, a = 10: b = 10 × sin 70° ÷ sin 55° = 11.47.

teach.heading: Finding an angle
teach.note: Check: since b < a, B is smaller than A ✓. Calculate: 7 × sin 65° ÷ 9 = 0.7049. Higher note: if the given angle is opposite the shorter side, two triangles may be possible (the ambiguous case).

teach.heading: Choosing a rule
bullets: Right angle: SOH CAH TOA or Pythagoras.
Side and opposite angle known: sine rule.
teach.note: Give pupils five triangle diagrams and ask them to choose the rule only. This decision is the harder skill.

practice: A = 40°, B = 65°, a = 8 cm. Find b to 2 d.p.
A = 50°, C = 70°, c = 12 cm. Find a.
a = 9, b = 7, A = 65°. Find B.
independent: Find b if A = 55°, B = 70° and a = 10.
In triangle ABC, a = 12, b = 9 and A = 80°. Find B.
In triangle PQR, P = 38°, Q = 77° and p = 9 cm. Find q.
lessons.homework: Draw and label four non-right-angled triangles, decide which rule applies to each, and solve two of them.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: labelled triangle templates with a matching-pair checklist. Stretch: investigate when two different triangles satisfy the same sine rule data.

lessons.title: The cosine rule
objectives: Use the cosine rule to find a side
Rearrange it to find an angle
Choose between sine and cosine rules

keywords.def: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A
the angle between two known sides
an angle greater than 90° and less than 180°

starter: Find θ if cos θ = 0.2 (1 d.p.).

teach.heading: When to use it
bullets: Two sides and the angle between them.
Or all three sides and you want an angle.
teach.note: If you know two sides and the included angle there is no pair for the sine rule. Compare with the sine rule list. The cosine rule is Pythagoras with a correction: when A = 90°, cos A = 0.

teach.heading: Finding a side
teach.note: Calculate the whole right-hand side before square rooting. Common error: working out 49 + 81 − 2 × 7 × 9 first and then multiplying by cos 60°. Use BIDMAS: 2 × 7 × 9 × cos 60° = 126 × 0.5 = 63.

teach.heading: Finding an angle
teach.note: Take the angle opposite the side that is squared on its own: C is opposite c = 7. A negative cosine means the angle is obtuse; for sides 8, 10, 13: cos = (64 + 100 − 169) ÷ 160 = −0.03125, so 91.8°.

teach.heading: Which rule?
bullets: AAS or ASA, or a side-angle pair: sine rule.
teach.note: Practise decisions again with five examples. Ask: can we use the sine rule for 5, 6, 7 triangle? No pair exists.

teach.heading: Applying
bullets: Two paths of 12 m and 15 m meet at 40°.
teach.note: 360 × cos 40° = 275.78. 369 − 275.78 = 93.22, √93.22 = 9.655, so 9.66 m. Link: surveying and navigation use these rules; the Muslim scholar al-Biruni used trigonometry to estimate the radius of the Earth.

practice: Find a: b = 7, c = 9, A = 60°.
Find C in a triangle with sides 5, 6 and 7.
Find the third side if two sides are 12 and 15 and the angle between them is 40°.
independent: Find the side opposite 110° when the other sides are 6 and 8.
Find the largest angle in a triangle with sides 9, 11 and 14.
In triangle ABC, a = 8, b = 5 and c = 10. Find angle A.
exit: Find x if b = 4, c = 5 and A = 90°. What do you notice?
lessons.homework: Complete five mixed sine and cosine rule problems, writing which rule you chose and why.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: formula card with a decision flow chart. Stretch: prove that cosine rule becomes Pythagoras' theorem when A = 90°.

lessons.title: Area of a triangle: ½ab sin C
objectives: Use area = ½ab sin C
Find an angle from an area
Solve combined problems with sine or cosine rule

keywords.def: the amount of surface inside a shape, in square units
the angle between the two known sides
the height measured at 90° to the base

starter: Calculate the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.

teach.heading: Where it comes from
teach.note: Draw a triangle with side a as base and drop a perpendicular. The height is b sin C. This formula is useful when height is not given. The angle must be between the two sides used.

teach.heading: Worked example
teach.note: ½ × 8 × 11 = 44, then 44 × sin 40° = 28.28. Units are squared. Check: a triangle with base 8 and height under 11 should have area less than 44 ✓.

teach.heading: Exact value
teach.note: When the angle is 30°, 45° or 60°, use the exact value of sin. Link to the next lesson on exact values. For 60° with sides 8 and 6 the area is 24 × √3/2 = 12√3.

teach.heading: Finding an angle
bullets: Area 30 cm², sides 10 cm and 12 cm.
teach.note: If C could be obtuse, there is a second solution 150°. Ask: what are the two angles whose sine is 0.5? (30° and 150°.) The diagram tells you which.

teach.heading: A field
bullets: Field with sides 120 m and 150 m, angle 70°.
teach.note: 9,000 × 0.9397 = 8,457. Convert to hectares: 0.85 ha (1 ha = 10,000 m²). Surveyors use this formula to find the area of land from measured sides and angles.

practice: Find the area: sides 8 and 11 with included angle 40°.
Find the area: sides 9 and 12 with included angle 30°.
Area 30 cm², sides 10 cm and 12 cm. Find angle C.
independent: Find the area of a triangle with sides 14 cm and 20 cm and included angle 125°.
A triangle has area 45 cm² and sides 15 cm and 8 cm. Find the acute angle between them.
Find the exact area of a triangle with sides 8 and 6 and included angle 60°.
exit: State the formula for the area of a triangle using two sides and the included angle.
Find the area with sides 7 cm and 10 cm and angle 50°.
lessons.homework: Create and solve a triangle area problem for a field or garden with sides you choose.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: labelled diagrams with the included angle highlighted. Stretch: find the area of a regular hexagon with side 6 cm by splitting into triangles.

lessons.title: Exact values of trigonometric functions
objectives: Recall exact values of sin, cos and tan for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90°
Derive them from equilateral and right-isosceles triangles
Use exact values in calculations without a calculator

keywords.def: an answer written using surds or fractions, not decimals
a triangle with three equal sides and three 60° angles
an irrational root such as √3

starter: Draw an equilateral triangle and state each angle.

teach.heading: The triangles
bullets: Equilateral triangle, side 2, cut in half.
teach.note: Height of the equilateral triangle: √(2² − 1²) = √3. The 30-60-90 triangle has sides 1, √3, 2. The 45-45-90 triangle has sides 1, 1, √2 by Pythagoras.

teach.heading: 30° and 60°
teach.note: Read the ratios off the 1, √3, 2 triangle. tan 30° = 1/√3 = √3/3 after rationalising. Ask: why is sin 30° = cos 60°? The opposite side to 30° is the adjacent side to 60°.

teach.heading: 45°, 0° and 90°
teach.note: 1/√2 = √2/2 after rationalising. Build a table on the board for pupils to learn. Tan 90° is undefined. A memory aid: sin counts up through 0, 1/2, √2/2, √3/2, 1 (written as √0/2, √1/2, √2/2, √3/2, √4/2).

teach.heading: Exact lengths
teach.note: Check the 45° hypotenuse: 6 ÷ cos 45° = 6 ÷ (√2/2) = 12/√2 = 6√2. Verify with Pythagoras: 6² + 6² = 72 = (6√2)² ✓.

teach.heading: Evaluating expressions
teach.note: No calculator. Show steps. The identity sin² + cos² = 1 is true for every angle. Exact area link: ½ × 8 × 6 × sin 60° = 12√3.

practice: Write down the exact value of sin 60°, cos 45° and tan 30°.
Find the exact height of an equilateral triangle with side 8 cm.
Calculate the exact value of tan 60° × tan 30°.
independent: Find the exact length of the side opposite the 60° angle when the hypotenuse is 12.
Calculate the exact value of cos 30° × sin 60° − sin 30°.
Solve sin θ = √3/2 for 0° < θ < 90°.
exit: Write the exact value of cos 45° × sin 30°.
A right-angled isosceles triangle has hypotenuse 10 cm. Find the equal side exactly.
lessons.homework: Draw the two special triangles and make a revision table of the exact values.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: pre-drawn triangles and a blank table of values to complete. Stretch: show that sin 60° = 2 sin 30° cos 30°.
